newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Frontline says settles future financing.
newsitem.headline: Frontline says settles future financing.

text.p: Scandinavian bulk shipping company Frontline Ltd said on Tuesday it had finalised financing agreements to take over the operations of Frontline AB as part of a programme to revitalise the company.
Frontline's Swedish operations, listed in Stockholm, are to be transferred to a new Bermuda-registered firm, Frontline Ltd, which is to be listed in Oslo next month.

"Frontline AB's current credit providers have confirmed that guarantees can be transferred from Frontline AB to Frontline Ltd for an existing credit facility of $420 million," the company said in a statement.

Frontline Ltd also has a credit facility for $100 million from a bank consortium led by Banque Paribas for refinancing three OBO-ships which are currently financed through a Swedish mortgage institute with credit totalling $98 million.

Frontline Ltd said it had earlier entered a binding credit agreement with Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse for a five-year credit facility for up to 222 million crowns to finance the purchase of convertible debentures in Frontline AB.
Frontline AB shareholders voted at a general meeting on June 13 to sell the company's operations to Frontline Ltd.
The offer period to exchange shares in Frontline AB for Frontline Ltd runs from June 2-27 and listing in Oslo was expected to take place on July 4.
Frontline Ltd is controlled by Norway's John Fredriksen.
Frontline AB shares were trading 0.5 crowns lower at 25.80 crowns at 1000 GMT on Tuesday.
